{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"831f9b23723b7bacbeb676cd7cff930fd14c1ea9e9833c54df19888ae055d971","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:60","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Visual search, speed and stopping","heading":"C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Visual search, speed and stopping","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Visual search, speed and stopping

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A50
On a long or steep downhill, check mirrors for vehicles gaining speed, especially large trucks or buses. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A50
The handbook highlights October and November for increased deer-crash vigilance. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A50
Be especially alert for deer at dawn and dusk, scanning the roadside for reflected headlight light in their eyes. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A50
If deer-eye reflections appear beside the road, slow, sound the horn, prepare to stop and look for more deer. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A50
Deer may cross at any time or place, including towns and cities rather than only rural areas. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A50
Safe speed management combines adjustment to road and traffic conditions, sufficient following space and compliance with speed limits. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A50
Slow to a safe curve speed before entering so slight, steady acceleration can be used through the curve. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A50
Reduce curve speed further when traction is poor, a vehicle is ahead or the curve’s end cannot be seen. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A50
Hard braking after entering a curve can break tire traction. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A50
Reduce speed at the first rain, snow, sleet or ice because reduced tire grip lengthens stopping and increases skidding risk in turns. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A50
Hydroplaning occurs when the steering tires ride onto pooled water, and slowing in rain or standing-water conditions helps prevent that traction loss. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A50
Do not drive through large standing-water areas on the road; use another route around flooding. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A50
Total stopping distance covers travel from recognizing a need to stop until the vehicle halts, under the stated ideal conditions. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A50
Higher travel speed increases the time and distance needed to stop. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A50
Perception time covers recognizing the need to stop, with the handbook giving an alert-driver average from three-quarters of a second to 1 second. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A50
Reaction time covers moving from the accelerator toward braking, with the handbook giving an average from three-quarters of a second to 1 second. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A50
Braking distance covers brake action to a stop; the handbook’s example is about 158 feet at 50 miles per hour on dry pavement with good brakes. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A51
A space cushion around the vehicle provides room and time to respond to other road users. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R19 | anchor: A51
Aim for a minimum following interval of 4 seconds because close following restricts forward vision and response time. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R20 | anchor: A51
Measure following time from when the preceding vehicle’s rear passes a fixed landmark until your vehicle reaches the same point. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R21 | anchor: A51
Reaching the landmark before counting 4 seconds means the interval is too short; slow and retest at another point until the minimum is met. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R22 | anchor: A51
Practice estimating an object’s time distance and then count the actual travel seconds to check the estimate. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R23 | anchor: A51
Leave more following space on slippery roads because stopping takes farther. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R24 | anchor: A51
When the following driver wants to pass, slow enough to open space ahead and help the pass finish sooner. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R25 | anchor: A51
Increase space behind motorcycles and bicycles to avoid a fallen rider, especially on wet, icy, gravel or metal surfaces. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R26 | anchor: A51
Stay farther behind drivers who cannot see you, such as operators of trucks, buses, vans or towing vehicles. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R27 | anchor: A51
The handbook says a large truck’s rear blind area can extend 200 feet, and dropping back also improves your forward view. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R28 | anchor: A51
Increase following space when carrying a heavy load or towing because the extra weight lengthens stopping. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R29 | anchor: A51
Allow extra following room in darkness or bad weather and when another vehicle follows you closely. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R30 | anchor: A51
Leave more space behind police vehicles, ambulances and fire trucks because they need room to operate. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R31 | anchor: A51
At rail crossings, leave extra room behind vehicles that must stop, including transit buses, school buses and hazardous-material carriers. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec14-R32 | anchor: A51
When stopped on an incline, allow extra space in case the vehicle ahead rolls backward on starting. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0051]
